title: North/South assembly meets in Leinster House for eleventh plenary
dek: Meeting in Leinster House for the first time in several years, the assembly discussed a range of health matters and the PEACEPLUS cross-Border funding programme.

hero.alt: The Co-Chairs of the NSIPA in a Leinster House corridor in May 2026

content.text: is a forum for regular formal discussions between Members of the Northern Ireland Assembly and the Houses of the Oireachtas on matters of mutual interest.

attrs.alt: The members of NSIPA on the steps of Leinster House
attrs.caption: Members of the NSIPA attending the May 2026 meeting.

content.text: The members of the NSIPA gathered on 22 May in the Seanad Chamber for its eleventh plenary session, chaired by the Ceann Comhairle, Deputy Verona Murphy, and the Co-Chair, Speaker Edwin Poots MLA. This meeting allowed members to discuss and assess the current position of matters relating to paediatric cancer, palliative care and paediatrics pathology and the PEACEPLUS programme, along with consideration of where further progress could be made.

The assembly was told of the need for data to better understand how many children could benefit from palliative care and that although positive initiatives demonstrate strong relationships at the clinical level, there is a need for stronger guidance and policy to break down barriers and realise the full potential that exists across the island of Ireland.

content.text: The assembly was told that the current €1.14 billion PEACEPLUS programme is approaching its halfway point, with more than 120 projects approved and benefits seen across areas such as community regeneration and the creation of shared spaces, the support of small and medium enterprises, innovation and skills development and environmental sustainability.
was highlighted as an innovative initiative that allows local communities to access funding through grants of up to €100,000 through a simplified rolling application process.
The Co-Chairs praised the contributions of the speakers, as they helped to shared two well-informed debates, with members of the assembly sharing personal experiences to enrich the discussion.
The NSIPA intends to meet next at Parliament Buildings in Stormont later in 2026.
